title: Generative design of bacteriophages with genome language models
methods: computational triage with phage genomics tooling (PHANOTATE, Prodigal, Bakta, geNomad, BLAST+)
de novo genome synthesis and phage rebooting in E. coli
phage cocktail challenge against resistant host strains
data_sources: NCBI Viral Genomes Resource / NCBI Datasets
curated phage genome size table (GitHub, nataquinones/phage_genome_size)

data_scope.design_template: bacteriophage PhiX174 (ssDNA microvirus of Escherichia coli)
data_scope.host_system: Escherichia coli laboratory strains, including PhiX174-resistant derivatives (strain count not stated)
data_scope.structural_validation: cryo-EM of one generated phage capsid; accession IDs not stated in retrievable metadata
data_scope.publisher_fulltext_access: HTTP 403 during harvesting; digest reconstructed from abstract + Crossref reference list

core_conclusion: A genome language model can write complete, viable bacteriophage genomes rather than single genes. Using PhiX174 as a design template, the authors generated whole phage genomes de novo and obtained 16 viable phages with target host tropism and diverse laboratory fitness profiles. Cryo-EM confirmed that one generated phage assembles its capsid with an evolutionarily distant DNA-packaging protein, and a cocktail of generated phages rapidly overcame PhiX174-resistant E. coli, outlining a path toward AI-generated phage therapies against rapidly evolving bacterial pathogens.
why_it_matters: Moves the unit of generative design from molecule to whole genome, with wet-lab rather than in-silico validation; the distant packaging protein is structural proof of genuine recombination beyond the training template; and it converts phage therapy from an environmental search problem into a generation problem aimed squarely at antimicrobial resistance, while explicitly engaging biosecurity governance.
why_nature: Why Science: a clean field-defining first (first generative design of complete phage genomes); computation closed by synthesis, phenotyping and cryo-EM; a mechanistic surprise rather than a benchmark score; immediate AMR translational stakes; and an explicit biosecurity/governance dimension that Science actively seeks.
added_value_to_my_research: Place-conditioned generation: wastewater/clinical resistome surfaces become geographically indexed design targets, giving my spatiotemporal surveillance maps an action layer
Phage-host coevolution embedded in networked SIR / agent-based models over ward-transfer and mobility graphs, turning a flask result into a rate-competition problem
Explainable viability surrogate with active learning - the same few-positive, expensive-label, attribution-first protocol I use for spatial prediction and geospatial foundation-model fine-tuning
Design-build-test-learn loop economics as a budget-constrained allocation problem, portable to my EV-charging efficiency-vs-equity and facility-siting optimization
2SFCA/R2SFCA accessibility modeling of who can actually receive personalized phage therapy, plus an environmental release-and-persistence exposure surface
